string.name: policy_title
string.value: Privacy Policy

string.name: policy_heading
string.value: SourceTime Privacy Policy

string.name: policy_version_label
string.value: Version %s

string.name: policy_effective_date
string.value: Effective date: October 16, 2026

string.name: policy_section_intro_title
string.value: 1. Introduction and Scope

string.name: policy_section_intro_body_1
string.value: SourceTime is a local-first TOTP authenticator for HarmonyOS that generates one-time verification codes on your device in accordance with RFC 6238.

string.name: policy_section_intro_body_2
string.value: This policy applies to all data processing inside the app, including data collection, encrypted local storage, runtime logs, WebDAV sync, clipboard use, and data deletion.

string.name: policy_section_intro_body_3
string.value: This policy covers the SourceTime app itself only. The WebDAV server you configure yourself and system-level capabilities such as the operating system clipboard are outside the scope of this policy; their data processing is governed by the rules of the respective providers.

string.name: policy_section_intro_body_4
string.value: SourceTime is an open-source app (MIT License). Its source code is available for review, and you can verify each of the statements in this policy by reviewing the code.

string.name: policy_section_purpose_title
string.value: 2. Purposes and Legal Basis of Data Processing

string.name: policy_section_purpose_body_1
string.value: SourceTime processes only the data necessary to provide its core functionality. It does not perform user profiling, targeted marketing, or behavioral analytics unrelated to its features.

string.name: policy_section_purpose_body_2
string.value: The purposes of processing are: generating TOTP verification codes locally on your device; encrypting and storing the code configuration and WebDAV configuration you enter; performing encrypted backup sync when you actively enable it; and retaining local logs for troubleshooting and diagnostics.

string.name: policy_section_purpose_body_3
string.value: The legal basis for processing is your explicit consent to this privacy policy when you first launch the app, together with the necessity of processing to provide the features you request; you may stop using the app and delete the related data at any time.

string.name: policy_section_purpose_body_4
string.value: SourceTime does not use your data for any other purpose not stated in this policy.

string.name: policy_section_data_title
string.value: 3. Data We Collect and Process

string.name: policy_section_data_body_1
string.value: SourceTime does not collect your personally identifiable information or upload it to us. It requires no registration or login and does not associate your phone number or email address. Data you enter is processed only locally on your device, and the developer holds no copy of it.

string.name: policy_section_data_body_2
string.value: SourceTime does not automatically collect device hardware identifiers (such as IMEI or OAID), location, contacts, call records, app usage statistics, or crash reports.

string.name: policy_section_data_body_3
string.value: The data you enter and store locally includes: TOTP configurations (issuer, account, secret, algorithm, digits, period), the encryption key, the verification value and salt derived from the app lock PIN (only when you enable the app lock), and the WebDAV connection configuration (server address, username, password, remote path, and sync switches).

string.name: policy_section_data_body_4
string.value: To identify the local database instance, the app stores a random UUID generated by the app itself (deviceId) in the encrypted vault. It is not any system hardware identifier and is not used to track your device or identity. It is stored only inside the encrypted vault (and travels with the ciphertext backup when sync is enabled) and is never uploaded separately to the developer or any third party.

string.name: policy_section_data_body_5
string.value: The app does not participate in the operating system's backup and restore process (allowToBackupRestore is disabled in its configuration), so the data described above is not included in system-level backups. Apart from the WebDAV sync you actively enable, no data is sent to any external server.

string.name: policy_section_permissions_title
string.value: 4. Permissions

string.name: policy_section_permissions_body_1
string.value: SourceTime requests only two system permissions: network access (ohos.permission.INTERNET) and camera access (ohos.permission.CAMERA).

string.name: policy_section_permissions_body_2
string.value: Network access is used only for the WebDAV sync you configure and enable yourself; when WebDAV is not enabled, the app makes no network connections.

string.name: policy_section_permissions_body_3
string.value: Camera access is used only when you go to the scan page yourself, in the foreground (when: inuse), to scan otpauth QR codes and add TOTP configurations.

string.name: policy_section_permissions_body_4
string.value: Scanning calls the system-provided scanning component (ScanKit) for framing and recognition; the app receives only the recognized QR code text. It does not save camera images and does not use the camera in the background.

string.name: policy_section_permissions_body_5
string.value: SourceTime does not request other permissions such as storage read/write, location, microphone, phone, SMS, or contacts.

string.name: policy_section_storage_title
string.value: 5. Local Storage and Encryption

string.name: policy_section_storage_body_1
string.value: All code data is stored as a single encrypted file, totp.db.enc, in the app's private directory.

string.name: policy_section_storage_body_2
string.value: Data is encrypted with AES-256-GCM before it is written to disk: a random 12-byte nonce and a 16-byte authentication tag are used, and the authentication tag must be verified when the data is read.

string.name: policy_section_storage_body_3
string.value: The encryption key is derived from your master key with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256: a random 16-byte salt, 100,000 iterations, producing a 256-bit key.

string.name: policy_section_storage_body_4
string.value: Writes are atomic: data is first written to a temporary file, flushed to disk, and size-checked before it is renamed over the original file; if the write fails, the original file is kept.

string.name: policy_section_storage_body_5
string.value: App settings are stored in the app's private storage. The WebDAV password is stored encrypted, while the WebDAV server address, username, remote path, and individual switches are stored in plaintext inside the app's private space.

string.name: policy_section_storage_body_6
string.value: If you enable the app lock, the app stores only the PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 verification value and random salt derived from the PIN, never the PIN itself in plaintext; the verification value is compared on this device only and never enters any network request.

string.name: policy_section_storage_body_7
string.value: The app never stores the encryption key, TOTP secrets, the app lock PIN, or the WebDAV password in plaintext in any file.

string.name: policy_section_secret_title
string.value: 6. Encryption Key and Security

string.name: policy_section_secret_body_1
string.value: The encryption key is managed by the system asset store (Asset Store Kit); the app does not save the key as a plaintext file.

string.name: policy_section_secret_body_2
string.value: The managed key is available after the device is unlocked (DEVICE_UNLOCKED): it cannot be read while the device is locked, so even if the device is taken by someone else while locked, the key cannot be silently retrieved.

string.name: policy_section_secret_body_3
string.value: On launch, the app retrieves the key from the system asset store to silently encrypt and decrypt local data.

string.name: policy_section_secret_body_4
string.value: Once the app lock is enabled, the code list is covered on cold start and when returning from the background, and can only be viewed after you enter the on-device PIN. The app lock is no substitute for the encryption key and cannot recover data if the key is forgotten.

string.name: policy_section_secret_body_5
string.value: SourceTime offers no server-side key recovery; once the key is lost, encrypted data can no longer be decrypted.

string.name: policy_section_notice_title
string.value: 7. Important Notes

string.name: policy_section_notice_body_1
string.value: 7.1 Keep your encryption key safe. SourceTime offers no server-side key recovery; if the key is lost, encrypted data can no longer be decrypted.

string.name: policy_section_notice_body_2
string.value: 7.2 After setting the key, back it up to a safe place (such as a password manager or offline storage) right away.

string.name: policy_section_notice_body_3
string.value: 7.3 WebDAV sync transfers encrypted files, and by default the app allows only https:// addresses to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks; if you turn on "Allow insecure connections" and use http:// instead, your credentials and the ciphertext are not protected in transit.

string.name: policy_section_logs_title
string.value: 8. Runtime Logs and Diagnostic Information

string.name: policy_section_logs_body_1
string.value: SourceTime keeps runtime logs locally for troubleshooting and diagnostics, and also writes them to the system log (hilog).

string.name: policy_section_logs_body_2
string.value: Logs are stored as an NDJSON file (sourcetime_logs.ndjson) in the app's private directory. At most 500 entries are kept; the oldest entries are discarded once that limit is exceeded.

string.name: policy_section_logs_body_3
string.value: Logs are stored locally only and are never uploaded to any server.

string.name: policy_section_logs_body_4
string.value: To make issues easier to locate, logs record the necessary connection context, such as the WebDAV server address, the sync directory and backup file names, HTTP status codes, data byte counts, and elapsed time; this information does not include account names, passwords, keys, or Basic credentials.

string.name: policy_section_logs_body_5
string.value: The local log file (sourcetime_logs.ndjson) and the system log (hilog) output both go through the same redaction process before being written or printed, replacing sensitive fields such as keys, passwords, tokens, and authorization information with ***; this redaction is rule-based and best-effort, and does not constitute an absolute guarantee that sensitive information will never appear.

string.name: policy_section_logs_body_6
string.value: Please note: the same (redacted) log content is also written to the system log (hilog), where other apps with the required permissions or debugging tools on the same device may be able to read it. If you plan to provide logs to others or to a third party, please review and clean up information such as addresses in them yourself.

string.name: policy_section_logs_body_7
string.value: You can view, filter by level, copy (the content is the redacted local log), or clear logs in Settings > Runtime Logs.

string.name: policy_section_logs_body_8
string.value: Clearing logs deletes only the log file and does not affect your code data or your WebDAV sync configuration.

string.name: policy_section_webdav_title
string.value: 9. WebDAV Sync and Remote Backup

string.name: policy_section_webdav_body_1
string.value: SourceTime communicates over the network through the server address you specify only when you have configured and enabled WebDAV yourself.

string.name: policy_section_webdav_body_2
string.value: What is uploaded is the vault file already encrypted with AES-256-GCM on your device (ciphertext). The server side can see only ciphertext and cannot read your TOTP data directly.

string.name: policy_section_webdav_body_3
string.value: Every push creates a timestamped snapshot file (sourcetime-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.enc) and does not overwrite earlier snapshots.

string.name: policy_section_webdav_body_4
string.value: By default, the app keeps the 10 most recent snapshots remotely and automatically cleans up older ones; it deletes only backup files named by the app itself and does not affect other files on the server.

string.name: policy_section_webdav_body_5
string.value: Sync is triggered when you push or pull manually, after codes are added or deleted, after settings change, after the encryption key changes, and automatically on app launch (the last two automatic behaviors can be turned off in settings).

string.name: policy_section_webdav_body_6
string.value: When pulling manually, you can choose a snapshot to restore from the remote backup list, and after a second confirmation that snapshot overwrites your local data; manual pull provides no rollback protection, so proceed with caution.

string.name: policy_section_webdav_body_7
string.value: Automatic pull on launch includes rollback protection: if the remote data version is older than the local version, the app refuses to overwrite.

string.name: policy_section_webdav_body_8
string.value: If sync fails, the app does not roll back your local changes.

string.name: policy_section_webdav_body_9
string.value: To write backups, the app creates the sync directory on the server you specify as needed (MKCOL); when the server returns an error, the app records a fragment of the response (up to 200 characters) in the local log to help locate the problem.

string.name: policy_section_webdav_body_10
string.value: Network requests use HTTP Basic authentication; credentials are placed only in the request header and are not written to logs.

string.name: policy_section_webdav_body_11
string.value: By default only https:// addresses are allowed: if you enter an http:// server address, the app blocks sync and prompts you to switch to https. You can also explicitly turn on "Allow insecure connections" on the WebDAV settings page; in that case your username, password, and ciphertext files are transmitted without TLS protection. You assume that risk yourself, so use it only on trusted networks.

string.name: policy_section_webdav_body_12
string.value: The WebDAV server is set up and managed by you. The developer operates no server for receiving your data and is not responsible for its security or availability.

string.name: policy_section_clipboard_title
string.value: 10. Clipboard and Session Data

string.name: policy_section_clipboard_body_1
string.value: When you tap a verification code card, the current code is copied to the system clipboard.

string.name: policy_section_clipboard_body_2
string.value: After an encryption key is generated, the app can copy the key to the system clipboard with a single tap.

string.name: policy_section_clipboard_body_3
string.value: On the runtime log page, the app can copy the (redacted) logs to the system clipboard.

string.name: policy_section_clipboard_body_4
string.value: The system clipboard is a system-wide shared area, and other apps may read its contents; be aware of this risk after copying the encryption key, and clear the clipboard promptly after use.

string.name: policy_section_clipboard_body_5
string.value: When you copy a verification code or an encryption key, the app marks the clipboard data as usable on the local device only, so it does not participate in cross-device clipboard sync.

string.name: policy_section_clipboard_body_6
string.value: When you copy the redacted logs, the system clipboard's default sharing behavior is used; if you have enabled cross-device clipboard sync in the system, the log content may be synced to other devices signed in with the same account. Please clear the clipboard promptly after use.

string.name: policy_section_transfer_title
string.value: 11. Cross-Border Data Transfer

string.name: policy_section_transfer_body_1
string.value: SourceTime itself does not transmit your data to the developer or any third party, and the developer operates no server for receiving your data.

string.name: policy_section_transfer_body_2
string.value: When you configure a WebDAV server yourself, the encrypted backup files are transmitted to that server; if the server is located outside your country/region, the relevant data is transferred abroad at your own choice.

string.name: policy_section_transfer_body_3
string.value: The recipient abroad, the storage location, and its data processing rules are determined by the service provider you choose yourself; the developer is not involved and has no control over them. Please confirm the server's location and the legal requirements applicable to you before configuring it.

string.name: policy_section_backup_title
string.value: 12. System Backup and Restore

string.name: policy_section_backup_body_1
string.value: SourceTime does not participate in the operating system's backup and restore process: allowToBackupRestore is disabled in the app's configuration, so your app data is not included in system-level backups and will not be restored across devices through vendor cloud services.

string.name: policy_section_backup_body_2
string.value: To sync across multiple devices, enable WebDAV sync yourself (only ciphertext is transferred); this is the only data transfer channel the app provides.

string.name: policy_section_sharing_title
string.value: 13. Data Sharing and Third-Party Components

string.name: policy_section_sharing_body_1
string.value: SourceTime never uploads your data to the developer or any third-party server; the WebDAV server you configure yourself is the only external recipient of your data.

string.name: policy_section_sharing_body_2
string.value: The app integrates no third-party analytics, advertising, or crash-reporting SDKs and performs no data tracking.

string.name: policy_section_sharing_body_3
string.value: The app uses only HarmonyOS system capabilities, including networking (NetworkKit), QR scanning (ScanKit), cryptography (CryptoArchitectureKit), the system asset store (AssetStoreKit), and the system clipboard; no third-party data processing services are involved.

string.name: policy_section_retention_title
string.value: 14. Data Retention and Deletion

string.name: policy_section_retention_body_1
string.value: Retention periods by data type are as follows: TOTP code data is kept until you delete it; runtime logs keep at most 500 entries, and the oldest entries are discarded automatically beyond that; the WebDAV configuration is removed when you uninstall the app or clear its data; remote snapshots keep the 10 most recent by default.

string.name: policy_section_retention_body_2
string.value: The local encrypted vault (totp.db.enc) is retained until you delete it.

string.name: policy_section_retention_body_3
string.value: Runtime logs keep at most 500 entries, and you can clear them at any time on the runtime log page.

string.name: policy_section_retention_body_4
string.value: Remote snapshots are kept by your WebDAV server; the app keeps the 10 most recent by default, and you can also delete them on the server side yourself.

string.name: policy_section_retention_body_5
string.value: App settings (including the privacy policy confirmation status and the sync configuration) are stored in the app's private storage and are removed when you uninstall the app or clear its data.

string.name: policy_section_retention_body_6
string.value: Code data deleted in the app cannot be recovered.

string.name: policy_section_retention_body_7
string.value: When the local encrypted file cannot be decrypted with the current key, the app renames it aside (.orphan-<timestamp>) and keeps it instead of physically deleting it; only the "Forgot the key" flow physically deletes the local ciphertext, and only after your confirmation.

string.name: policy_section_retention_body_8
string.value: Uninstalling the app normally clears the app's private data; the app does not participate in system backups, so no data will be restored by the system from a backup.

string.name: policy_section_rights_title
string.value: 15. Your Rights

string.name: policy_section_rights_body_1
string.value: Access: you can view your saved codes and settings in the app at any time.

string.name: policy_section_rights_body_2
string.value: Correction: you can edit or re-enter any TOTP entry and modify the WebDAV configuration.

string.name: policy_section_rights_body_3
string.value: Deletion: you can delete code data, clear runtime logs, and remove the WebDAV configuration.

string.name: policy_section_rights_body_4
string.value: Withdrawal of consent: you can choose "Disagree" on first launch; once you have agreed, you can withdraw your consent by uninstalling the app or clearing the app data, after which the app will no longer process your data.

string.name: policy_section_rights_body_5
string.value: Key and sync control: you can change the encryption key and enable or disable WebDAV sync at any time.

string.name: policy_section_minors_title
string.value: 16. Protection of Minors

string.name: policy_section_minors_body_1
string.value: SourceTime is intended for users with full civil capacity and does not provide standalone services to children under 14 years of age.

string.name: policy_section_minors_body_2
string.value: The app does not collect or process the personal information of minors under 14. If a guardian discovers that a minor has used this app without consent, they can contact us through the channel below, and we will take measures to delete the relevant information.

string.name: policy_section_security_title
string.value: 17. Information Security and Incident Response

string.name: policy_section_security_body_1
string.value: SourceTime adopts technical measures such as encrypted local storage, entrusting the key to the system asset store, atomic writes, and log redaction to reduce the risk of unauthorized access or damage to your data.

string.name: policy_section_security_body_2
string.value: Because data is stored as ciphertext on your device and on the server you configure yourself, the developer holds no copy of your data and operates no server for receiving it.

string.name: policy_section_security_body_3
string.value: If you discover or suspect that your key, ciphertext, or account credentials have been leaked, we recommend immediately changing the encryption key, disabling WebDAV sync, and rotating credentials on your WebDAV server and with the relevant 2FA providers.

string.name: policy_section_security_body_4
string.value: If you find a security issue in the app's code itself, please report it through the project repository; we will verify it and fix it as soon as possible.

string.name: policy_section_updates_title
string.value: 18. Privacy Policy Updates and Consent

string.name: policy_section_updates_body_1
string.value: This policy may be revised as new versions of the app are released.

string.name: policy_section_updates_body_2
string.value: The policy version number is recorded in the app settings; you can view the current version and effective date at the top of this page and in Settings > Privacy Policy at any time.

string.name: policy_section_updates_body_3
string.value: If the policy changes materially, the app will show the privacy confirmation dialog again on the next launch and ask for your explicit consent once more.

string.name: policy_section_updates_body_4
string.value: If you do not agree to the updated policy, you can stop using the app and uninstall it.

string.name: policy_section_law_title
string.value: 19. Governing Law and Dispute Resolution

string.name: policy_section_law_body_1
string.value: This policy is governed by the laws of the People's Republic of China.

string.name: policy_section_law_body_2
string.value: Any dispute arising from this policy shall first be settled through friendly negotiation between the parties; if negotiation fails, either party may file a lawsuit with a people's court that has jurisdiction.

string.name: policy_section_contact_title
string.value: 20. Contact Us

string.name: policy_section_contact_body_1
string.value: SourceTime is maintained by an individual developer and has no dedicated data protection officer.

string.name: policy_section_contact_body_2
string.value: If you have any questions, requests, or complaints about this policy or about how your data is processed, please open an Issue in the project repository: https://github.com/BG7ZAG/source-time/issues

string.name: policy_section_contact_body_3
string.value: You can also learn more about how data is processed by reviewing the open-source code (MIT License).

string.name: policy_footer_note
string.value: If you have any questions about this policy, please open an Issue in the project repository.
